clue.text: Stop the car to put on Jersey?

definitions.meaning: a driver halting draws in to the roadside
a jersey is a knitted woollen top; the question mark hints it is not the island

explanation.surface: A motorist halts in order to get on a ferry to Jersey.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey looks like the Channel Island, off the French coast, but it is the knitted garment you put on.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing in to the kerb is the driving phrase, and a jersey is a sweater worn over the head.

clue.text: For the time being, make a note during concert

indicators.note: during places the note inside the concert, as one thing happening within another

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone is told to jot something down while a concert is on.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin abbreviation means temporarily, for the present only.

clue.text: A diplomat in Senegal, eg, a temporary placement

indicators.note: in signals the answer sits within the run of clue words that follows it

explanation.surface: An envoy is posted to Senegal on a short-term assignment.
explanation.definitionFit: A papal envoy or ambassador sent on a mission bears this title.

clue.text: They admit it's theirs

parts.note: read first as people who confess, as to own up is to admit; then as people who possess something and claim it

explanation.definitionFit: Possessors claim things as theirs, and to own up is to admit.

clue.text: Hard point for listeners to take in on Norfolk folk?

indicators.note: to take in means the listeners' word swallows the other pieces whole

parts.note: ears are the organs we listen with
stern means hard or severe
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A harsh lesson for an audience to absorb about the people of Norfolk.
explanation.walkthrough: Norfolk is a county in East Anglia, in eastern England, so its people are an example, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: People from Norfolk live in the east of England, so they are an example of people from that region.

clue.text: Unwilling workers who wash aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard puts the washing word inside the ship abbreviation, as cargo is carried on a vessel

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
lave is a literary word for wash

explanation.surface: Forced labourers scrub the decks on board a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: People held in bondage labour against their will.

clue.text: Uniformed ranks I deliver

indicators.note: ranks, as a verb meaning arranges in order, signals the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A uniformed soldier in the ranks says he delivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Servants and footmen in household costume wear a distinctive outfit.

clue.text: Truthfulness of the forces' sweetheart on Leeds, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: Dame Vera Lynn, the wartime singer, was known as the Forces' Sweetheart
Leeds is an example of a city

explanation.surface: Questioning the honesty of a wartime singer performing in Leeds.
explanation.walkthrough: Vera Lynn sang to British troops in the Second World War; Leeds is a city in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Honesty, the habit of telling things as they really are.

clue.text: Speedy is one way to describe this salmon-fishing area

definitions.text: Speedy is one way to describe this salmon-fishing area

parts.words: Speedy is one way to describe this salmon-fishing area
parts.note: a playful reading: the word Speedy is a Scottish river's name with ED slipped inside it, a riddling description of the district

explanation.walkthrough: SPEEDY is SPEY with ED inside; the River Spey in north-east Scotland is famous for salmon.
explanation.definitionFit: The valley of the River Spey in north-east Scotland is renowned for salmon angling and whisky.

clue.text: He pulls out all the stops when performing!

definitions.text: He pulls out all the stops when performing!

parts.words: He pulls out all the stops when performing!
parts.note: the idiom for making every effort is taken literally: the stops are knobs that bring in ranks of pipes on a church instrument

explanation.definitionFit: A church musician at the keyboard draws stops to sound the pipes.

clue.text: English states at first reluctant

indicators.note: at first places the word for states ahead of the abbreviation for English

parts.note: avers means states firmly

explanation.surface: An English person declares they were initially unwilling.
explanation.definitionFit: Being opposed to something makes one unwilling to do it.

clue.text: Get into Yale, possibly, as computer controller

parts.note: to enter is to get into
Yale is a brand of lock, and one of these opens it

explanation.surface: A student's admission to Yale University is decided by a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: Yale looks like the university, but it is the lock brand.
explanation.definitionFit: The return button on a keyboard submits commands to a computer.

clue.text: Signs of second steroid used at track events

indicators.note: second picks out the second letter of the word steroid that follows

parts.note: races are events held on an athletics track

explanation.surface: Evidence of a steroid being used at an athletics meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Faint marks or indications left behind are vestiges of something.

clue.text: Rushing away after meal — band is cancelled

parts.note: tea is an afternoon or evening meal in Britain
a ring is a circular band
an event called off is said to be off

explanation.surface: Hurrying away after dinner because the band's gig has been called off.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashing off at high speed.

clue.text: Concerned with profit at the end — not new!

parts.note: interest is the profit earned on money lent

indicators.note: not removes the abbreviation for new from the word end

explanation.surface: Someone cares about making money in the end, but not about novelty.
explanation.definitionFit: Being concerned means having a stake or involvement in something.

clue.text: The organ needs something added

definitions.meaning: the small vestigial pouch attached to the large intestine
a supplementary section at the back of a book

explanation.surface: The body part needs an extra piece.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the small intestinal pouch; the other is a supplement at the end of a book.

clue.text: What a blonde has is just a shock!

parts.note: fair means just or equitable
a shock is a thick bushy mop on the head

explanation.surface: A blonde's reaction is pure surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A blonde has light-coloured locks.

clue.text: Prevent child worker joining strike

parts.note: to stop is to prevent
a page is a boy employed as an attendant or messenger

explanation.surface: Union members try to end child labour by joining a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkout, when workers down tools, is an industrial halt.

clue.text: They cover the walls and later press for repairs

indicators.note: for repairs suggests the letters are taken apart and put back together in a fixed form

explanation.surface: Decorators coat the walls and then iron the clothes that need mending.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradesmen who apply a smooth coat of lime or gypsum to walls and ceilings.

clue.text: First letter with complaint I received on rodent

parts.note: A is the first letter of the alphabet
gout is a painful medical complaint

explanation.surface: Someone with gout writes about a rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: This South American animal, related to the guinea pig, belongs to the gnawing order of mammals.

clue.text: A magical land — in Aran perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the words in Aran could be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: Wondering if a magical land might be found in the Aran Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The Aran Islands lie off the west coast of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: C S Lewis's fictional realm, reached through a wardrobe.

clue.text: A smoker's necessity, not hard to see it's misplaced

indicators.note: not takes away the letter for hard from the smoker's dish

parts.note: an ashtray is where a smoker taps ash
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone can't find the dish they need for their cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gone missing has wandered off the right path.

clue.text: In ecstasy when pop music is played in hospital department?

indicators.note: played in puts the music inside the department, as a radio plays in a room

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
rap is a style of pop music

explanation.surface: A blissful mood when pop music plays on a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Carried away with delight, utterly entranced.

clue.text: Like 6, they need to be given fresh orders

definitions.text: Like 6, they need to be given fresh orders

parts.words: Like 6, they need to be given fresh orders
parts.note: 6 down's answer is built by jumbling the letters of its clue; such words have their letters put into new orders

explanation.walkthrough: 6 down's answer comes from rearranging I DELIVER, so it is an example; 'orders' looks like commands but means sequences of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Word puzzles made by jumbling letters into a new sequence, as 6 down's clue does.

clue.text: Plays with tot for a second

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: Someone plays while sipping a quick nip of whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage plays are theatrical works.

clue.text: A firm chimney — oddly neat, right? Like a pillar

parts.note: Co. abbreviates company, a firm
lum is a Scottish word for chimney

indicators.note: oddly takes the first and third letters of neat, those in odd positions

explanation.surface: A company's chimney is strangely tidy and upright, like a pillar.
explanation.walkthrough: LUM is Scots for chimney; 'A' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaped as an upright cylindrical column.

clue.text: Reject intimacy with king, a Persian king

indicators.note: reject means throw back, so the combined pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: sex is physical intimacy
rex is Latin for king

explanation.surface: A Persian monarch spurns a royal's advances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reject' turns SEXREX round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The Achaemenid ruler who invaded Greece in 480 BC.

clue.text: Competence needed to sort out loveless office, a heartlessly catty place

indicators.note: to sort out means put the remaining letters of office into a new order
loveless removes the letter shaped like zero, love in tennis scoring, from office
heartlessly removes the middle of catty, keeping only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An office full of spiteful colleagues needs reorganising to work well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' drops O from OFFICE; 'to sort out' rearranges FFICE as EFFIC; 'heartlessly' leaves CY from catty.
explanation.definitionFit: The capacity to produce the desired result, effectiveness.
